items.title: The front end owns the tape: 2Y +13bp vs 30Y +8bp, and the 50bp-hike tail went 0% to 15% in two sessions
items.idea: First cash session after the hot October CPI: the 2-year rose 13bp while the 30-year rose 8bp, 5s30s flattened 6bp to +48bp. Waller said 50bp belongs on the table if core CPI printed 0.3%+; it did, and futures moved the half-point tail from nothing to 15%. The 5Y nominal at 4.958% is back at its 2023 high on a monthly chart going back to 2000; 5Y real yield 2.625% reclaimed all three moving averages. Dauber's call: front end 60/40 over growth, wrong if the 2Y closes under 4.75%.
items.angle: If the front end is repricing 2027 rather than December, the trade is in 2Y and in anything priced off 5Y real (net lease, builders, long-duration biotech) rather than the index, which has round-tripped to June.
items.tweetA: The 5-year is at 4.96%, its 2023 high, on a chart going back to 2000. Meanwhile the S&P is exactly where it was in June. One of these two is not doing the math on 2027.
items.tweetB: A 15% chance of a 50bp hike didn't exist 48 hours ago. When the tail moves that fast, the market isn't pricing December. It's pricing the possibility that the Fed has lost the anchor and has to prove it. $TLT $IEF

charts.desc: 5-year nominal yield monthly since 2000 back at 2023 high with oscillator turning up; 5Y real yield vs moving averages; building materials (copper +150%, aluminum +95% vs CPI +30% since Feb 2020).

items.title: Nvidia is a funding story now: $108.5B of guarantees and $279B of supply commitments behind the GPU orders
items.idea: Dauber tallies the web the share price doesn't show: a $99B equity book, $108.5B of guarantees, $56B of cloud buy-backs and $279B of supply commitments across OpenAI, Anthropic, CoreWeave, Nscale, Nebius, Lambda and others; most of that money comes back as GPU orders. Huang resigned as CEO and director with no reason given; Colette Kress interim CEO, Harvey Jones first board chair. 'The governance question is answered and the balance sheet question has just been asked.' Wrong if NVDA closes under 148.80.
items.angle: The interim CEO who reportedly resisted backstops (WSJ, via P Equity) now controls the guarantee book. Neocloud credit (CRWV, NBIS debt) is the transmission channel to watch, not NVDA's P/E.
items.tweetA: $99B equity book. $108.5B in guarantees. $56B cloud buy-backs. $279B supply commitments. Add those up and Nvidia is a vendor-finance bank with a GPU attached, and the new CEO is the one who reportedly didn't like writing the guarantees. $NVDA $CRWV $NBIS
items.tweetB: The cleanest Nvidia question for Tuesday isn't guidance. It's whether Kress renews the backstops. If she doesn't, neocloud orders shrink and the 'demand' line gets a lot more honest.

charts.desc: Nvidia funding commitments table across neocloud and lab counterparties.

items.title: Credit refuses to confirm: HY tightened to 330bp while the 10Y broke 5.05% and the 30Y auction tailed
items.idea: Thursday's $25B 30-year auction tailed: 2.36 bid-to-cover vs 2.44 average, dealers took 11.4% vs 9.5%. Yet high yield printed 330bp, 4bp tighter, and the IG fund fell almost twice as much as the HY fund, which is duration, not a credit scare. Dauber: 'I can't fully reconcile a 10-year through 5.05% with an index that refuses to go down and a credit spread that keeps tightening.'
items.angle: Spreads tightening while the risk-free rate rises means all-in yields are doing the work. That holds until refinancing walls hit; FTAV's 'end of cheap money is coming for corporate America' chart is the other side of this.
items.tweetA: 30Y auction tails, dealers eat 11.4%, 10Y through 5.05%, and high yield tightens 4bp. Credit is the only market acting like nothing happened. Either it knows something or it's the last to find out. $HYG $LQD
items.tweetB: IG fell almost twice as much as HY on Thursday. That's not fear, that's duration. The day HY starts outperforming because spreads, not rates, are moving is the day this changes character. $JNK

items.title: Oil is a policy price again: IEA counts a 2 mb/d October surplus and Brent still went back over $95 on a social post
items.idea: The IEA has October supply running almost 2 million barrels a day over demand, the first surplus since the Iran war began, and Brent rose anyway, back over $95 on a social media post. Diesel at a record $6.40/gal. Dauber is wrong if Brent settles under $92.50. Separately, the UK sanctioned all ten of Russia's largest oil producers.
items.angle: A surplus market trading at war-premium prices is a pure headline-convexity setup. Good for owning optionality (calls on crude, straddles) rather than outright length.
items.tweetA: 2 mb/d surplus per the IEA. Brent up anyway on a post. When fundamentals say down and price says up, you aren't trading oil, you're trading the President's phone. Size accordingly. $USO $XLE
items.tweetB: Diesel at a record $6.40 while the IEA counts a surplus in crude. That gap is refining and logistics, not barrels, and it's why the inflation print keeps surprising even when oil 'should' be falling. $VLO $MPC

items.title: Trump pulls Vance off Iran, third carrier group nears position, Iran's cyber ops shift to physical damage
items.idea: Vance was moved from the Iran file to 'crime and corruption in Democratic cities'; Trump wrote the US has Iran's money and 'their Strait'. Rubio calls Iran intractable, a third carrier group is nearing its operational position, Iran's Guards claim a strike on a US early-warning radar in Bahrain and four tankers near Hormuz (unconfirmed). WSJ: Iranian cyber operations have moved to a wider target set and real-world damage. Dauber: 'My spidey sense is tingling.'
items.angle: Read with Bulltard's weekend-restart rumor and Mando's 'IAEA lost track of Iran's uranium': the market has three separate escalation signals on one day while VIX is only just over 20.
items.tweetA: Mediator removed. Third carrier group in position. IAEA can't find the uranium. Iran's cyber unit moving to physical targets. Each alone is noise. Together it's a weekend I wouldn't want to be short vol into. $VIX $USO
items.tweetB: Nobody prices cyber in the oil risk premium. If Iran's operations really have moved to 'real-world damage', the tail isn't just Hormuz tankers, it's a refinery or a pipeline SCADA system somewhere nobody's watching.

items.title: Cisco's hyperscaler AI guide: $9B vs $4B a year ago; Applied sees WFE growing >30%
items.idea: Cisco revenue +24% to $18.52B (vs $18.13B est), FY guide raised to $74.8-75.8B from $72.2-73.4B, AI infrastructure sales to hyperscalers guided to $9B vs $7.5B prior and $4B a year ago. Applied Materials posted a record $10.41B quarter, guided January to $11.10B and sees wafer fab equipment growing above 30%. Dauber: equipment names are a better way to own hyperscaler capex than the GPU vendor that just lost its founder. The semis-plus-neoclouds basket is flat on the year after a 350% peak in May.
items.angle: Supplier data says the capex cycle is intact while the GPU leader is in a governance crisis: a rotation within AI infra, not out of it.
items.tweetA: Cisco's AI sales to hyperscalers: $4B a year ago, $9B guided now. Applied sees WFE +30%. The capex cycle didn't break this week, Nvidia's management did. Those are different trades. $CSCO $AMAT $NVDA
items.tweetB: Semis + neoclouds basket: +350% at the May peak, flat on the year now. That's an entire bubble and unwind in six months, while the suppliers' order books went up. Price and fundamentals have fully decoupled in both directions. $SMH

items.title: The case against the hike: existing home sales at a 16-year low, record 40% expect worse finances, breakevens stopped reacting
items.idea: October existing home sales fell to a 16-year low, claims rose to 200k, and a record near 40% of Americans expect their finances to be worse in a year. Diesel at $6.40 and 7.11% mortgages are tightening before the Fed moves. Robin Brooks: another 50-100bp would do little to inflation; SF Fed work says breakevens stopped reacting to policy surprises by June 2026. The Russell didn't print above prior settle once in 6.5 hours on a 12bp 10Y move.
items.angle: If breakevens no longer respond to policy, hikes become a pure growth tax. Short housing-adjacent names until the 10Y is back under 4.80% (Dauber).
items.tweetA: SF Fed's own research: breakevens stopped reacting to policy surprises by June. If hikes no longer move inflation expectations, what exactly is a 50bp hike buying besides a recession in housing? $XHB $ITB
items.tweetB: 16-year low in existing home sales, record share of households expecting worse finances, and the Fed is debating 25 vs 50. 2022 rhymes: hike into a supply shock while the consumer rolls over. $IWM

items.title: MSCI will remove bitcoin treasury companies from its indexes as 'investment funds'; Strategy -6.5%
items.idea: Strategy fell 6.5% after MSCI said it will remove bitcoin treasury companies from its indexes on the view that they function as investment funds. Same session: Kalshi got regulator blessing to let users bet on stocks (CME and Cboe unhappy); Treasury opened fiscal 2027 with a record $404B October deficit.
items.angle: Index exclusion kills the passive bid that made the treasury-company premium self-reinforcing. Combine with Nakamoto's debt exceeding its market cap (Unchained) and the DAT model looks broken.
items.tweetA: MSCI just said what everyone knew: a bitcoin treasury company is a fund. Remove the passive bid and the mNAV premium has nothing holding it up. $MSTR at -6.5% is the first leg, not the last.
items.tweetB: Kalshi gets the nod to let you bet on stocks the same week MSCI kicks bitcoin treasuries out of equity indexes. The line between 'security' and 'wager' is being redrawn in both directions at once. $MSTR $CME $CBOE

items.title: Fun fact: Nvidia joined the S&P 500 on Nov 30, 2001, replacing Enron
items.idea: 25 years ago Nvidia was added to the S&P 500 as the replacement for Enron. Dauber frames Nvidia as 'the new poster child for the cockroach theory: there is never just one cockroach', with Republicans already summoning Huang to testify. Also notes the post-midterm base rate: the S&P has averaged +15.1% in the 12 months after the 19 midterms since 1950, +15.5% when a GOP president faced a Democratic Congress.
items.angle: Historical rhyme that writes itself, and a useful counterweight: the midterm seasonal argues against the bear case.
items.tweetA: Nvidia entered the S&P 500 in 2001 by replacing Enron. 25 years later the conversation is about off-balance-sheet guarantees and a CEO exit. History doesn't repeat, but it does keep the seating chart. $NVDA
items.tweetB: Post-midterm base rate: S&P +15.1% over 12 months across 19 midterms since 1950. Every bear thesis this month has to beat that number, and the historical record says most don't.

items.title: BTC loses $70K: $1.65B liquidated in 24h, 88.9% of it longs; spot ETFs shed $1.88B in November
items.idea: Bitcoin slid to $67,555 on Coinbase, -6.7% in 24h and -9.4% on the week; ETH -5.7% to $1,931. CoinGlass: $1.65B liquidated, 88.9% from longs. The 10Y hit 5.10% the same day. CoinShares' base case was a $70-90K range into 2027; James Butterfill: 'we should not assume it represents a hard floor.' Spot BTC ETFs -$1.88B month-to-date.
items.angle: Bitcoin is trading as a real-rate asset: the leg down coincided with the 10Y through 5.1%. Watch 5Y real yield, not on-chain metrics.
items.tweetA: $1.65B liquidated, 89% longs, on the day the 10Y printed 5.10%. Bitcoin isn't digital gold in this tape, it's the longest-duration risk asset on the board. $BTC $IBIT
items.tweetB: CoinShares' 2027 base case was $70-90K. Week one of the new range and we're under the floor. When the house research says 'don't assume it's a hard floor', believe them. $BTC

items.title: Trump sends first bipartisan SEC/CFTC slate, racing a Democratic Senate that arrives in January
items.idea: Four nominations on Nov 12: Democrat Kristin Johnson and Republican Steven Levine for the SEC; Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland for the CFTC. Johnson argued in 2023 that DeFi intermediaries 'can and should be regulated'. Levine would take Hester Peirce's seat. Both CFTC picks worked on the Clarity Act. CFTC is currently run solely by Chairman Mike Selig.
items.angle: A bipartisan slate is the price of confirmation before January; it also means the next SEC has a DeFi-skeptic Democrat seated. Crypto's regulatory tailwind is about to get a headwind component.
items.tweetA: First bipartisan SEC/CFTC picks of this administration, sent with weeks left before Democrats take the Senate. That's not outreach, that's a deadline. And one of the Democrats wrote that DeFi 'can and should be regulated'. $COIN $HOOD
items.tweetB: The CFTC has been a one-person commission. Whoever fills those seats will write the rules for prediction markets just as Kalshi raises at $65B. Watch the confirmation hearings, not the token charts.

items.title: Binance hack: DPRK took ~$6.3B, DOJ restrains $1.2B, and Binance's USDT reserve sits at 104.34%
items.idea: DOJ says North Korean unit TraderTraitor took more than $6B from Binance on or about Oct 29; a court authorized seizing or restraining $1.2B, part of $2.7B frozen across government and private efforts. Binance says all ~$6.34B is covered ('100%', Yi He) but the ZK proof customers need hasn't been generated. Proof of Reserves: BTC 100.05%, ETH 100.02%, USDT 104.34%, about 1.06B more USDT than customer balances. Separately, FaceStealer webcam-deepfake scheme linked to $400M+ theft.
items.angle: A $6B hack absorbed in two weeks is either proof of enormous unreported equity at Binance or of balance-sheet engineering. The ZK proof timing is the tell.
items.tweetA: Binance lost ~$6.3B to North Korea and says it's 100% covered two weeks later. If true, that's one of the most profitable private companies on earth. If you can't verify it yet, it's a press release. Watch for the ZK proof date. $BNB
items.tweetB: Less than half of the $6B DPRK haul is frozen. The rest funds a sanctioned weapons program. Crypto's biggest geopolitical story this year isn't ETFs, it's that North Korea runs one of the most successful hedge funds in the world.

items.title: Plumbing week: DTCC tokenization adds Solana, Visa settles in Western Union's USDPT, BNY offers staking
items.idea: DTCC will connect its tokenization service (live Oct 28) to Solana in 2H27, the fifth network on its roadmap. Western Union's USDPT, minted by Anchorage's federally chartered bank, is now a VisaNet settlement option alongside five other stablecoins. BNY tapped Figment validators for custody staking. Securitize and Ethena opened a 24/7 BUIDL-to-USDC swap facility ($50M, scalable to $100M). SoFiUSD went live on Polygon. KPMG audited Tether Gold ($2.2B allocated gold).
items.angle: While BTC breaks $70K, the institutional settlement layer keeps getting built. The price and the plumbing are on different cycles.
items.tweetA: Same week BTC breaks $70K: DTCC adds Solana, Visa settles in a Western Union stablecoin, BNY turns on staking. Price is in a bear market. Infrastructure is in a bull market. Only one of those is reversible. $SOL $V
items.tweetB: A 24/7 swap between BlackRock's money fund and USDC means T-bills now trade on weekends. That's not a crypto story, it's the end of the 5-day settlement week for cash management.

items.title: Kalshi in talks at $65B, weeks after raising at $40B, with money earmarked for a compute futures platform
items.idea: Bloomberg reports Kalshi is raising at a $65B valuation weeks after a $1B round at $40B; Reuters says proceeds would go toward a compute futures platform. Kalshi ended its advisory arrangement with Donald Trump Jr. (who advises rival Polymarket) a week after Democrats won both chambers; Warren lists prediction markets as an early oversight target and Louisiana is suing prediction markets.
items.angle: A regulated futures market for GPU-hours would let neoclouds and labs hedge the exact price risk that just blew up Nvidia's financing web. That's a real product, not a novelty.
items.tweetA: Kalshi +62% in valuation in a few weeks to fund compute futures. If GPU-hour pricing gets a forward curve, neocloud lenders finally get a hedge, and the 'circular financing' debate gets a market price. $NVDA $CRWV
items.tweetB: Prediction market raises at $65B the same week Democrats name it an oversight target and Louisiana sues. Valuation is pricing the product; nobody is pricing the regulator.

items.title: Nakamoto's debt ($165M USDT to Kraken) now exceeds its ~$104M market value
items.idea: Bitcoin treasury firm Nakamoto amended its Kraken loan, pushing $60M of $165M USDT debt to December 2027 with $105M still due June 30, 2027. The debt is more than its roughly $104M market value. Also: Gemini Q3 trading volume -73% y/y to $4.5B, revenue -19% to $40.9M.
items.angle: First treasury company where creditors effectively own the equity. Pair with MSCI's exclusion decision: the DAT capital stack is inverting.
items.tweetA: Nakamoto owes Kraken $165M and is worth $104M. A bitcoin treasury company where the lender owns more of the upside than the shareholders. That's the bear-market version of the 2025 playbook.
items.tweetB: Gemini volume -73% y/y. Treasury companies trading below debt. MSCI kicking them out of indexes. The crypto equity layer is deleveraging faster than the coin itself. $GEMI $MSTR

items.title: BTC ETF flows swung 75K BTC in six weeks: rolling 30-day from +50K to -25K
items.idea: Bitcoin lost its 200-day for the second failed recovery (first in May). Rolling 30-day ETF flows went from ~+50K BTC in late September to ~-25K today, a 75K BTC reversal in net demand. The drawdown is 13+ months, ~55% max, ~390 days in; similar-depth episodes typically take 1-1.5 years to recover the high. Bear scenario: below $60K by end of November.
items.angle: ETF flow is the marginal buyer; until the 30-day stops falling, rallies are exits. The Nasdaq briefly lost its 200-day too, so this is a risk-appetite problem, not crypto-specific.
items.tweetA: 75,000 BTC of net ETF demand reversed in six weeks. At $68K that's ~$5B of buying that turned into selling. No on-chain metric matters while that number is pointing down. $IBIT $BTC
items.tweetB: 390 days into a 55% drawdown. History says 1-1.5 years to reclaim the high. We're at the benchmark and nowhere close. The question isn't 'when bottom', it's whether this cycle runs longer than the playbook.

charts.desc: Rolling 30-day BTC ETF flows from +50K to -25K BTC; BTC vs 200-day MA alongside Nasdaq; drawdown duration vs historical episodes.

items.title: 10Y at 5.15% pre-PPI; China's October credit data weaker than expected ahead of the Trump-Xi summit
items.idea: Pre-PPI: 10-year up 4bp to 5.15%, Bitcoin -3% to $69K, gold and crude flat. Headline PPI came in a tenth light, core in line, and futures added gains. Asia: Hong Kong -1.6%, Kospi -1.0%, Japan +1% on uncertainty over US tech-export policy ahead of next week's Trump-Xi summit; China's new loans and money supply for October missed, suggesting stimulus isn't biting. Eurozone Q3 GDP +0.4% q/q in line, employment +0.1% vs 0.2%.
items.angle: A Trump-Xi summit landing in the middle of an Nvidia export-control scandal is the key event risk for Asian tech next week.
items.tweetA: Trump-Xi summit next week, Nvidia smuggling scandal this week, China credit data missing. Hard to see Beijing getting chip concessions now, and Hong Kong's -1.6% says the market agrees. $FXI $BABA
items.tweetB: 10Y at 5.15% and the S&P futures are green on an in-line core PPI. The bar for 'good news' is now 'not worse'. That's how late-cycle tapes feel.

items.title: Microsoft 365 outage forced Japanese markets onto fax machines
items.idea: Mando's AI & Tech list: a widespread Microsoft 365 outage forced Japan markets into fax, Claude hit outages ahead of the IPO, TSMC says its systems are safe after a staff data leak. Also: Arm's share of hyperscaler servers has tripled since 2024; Cerebras surged pre-market on guidance; Tesla and SpaceX could merge by December; SpaceX plans a ~$50B AI campus in Arizona.
items.angle: Single-vendor concentration risk in financial plumbing: a cloud outage reverts a G7 market to 1980s tech. That's an operational-resilience regulation story waiting to happen.
items.tweetA: A Microsoft outage pushed Japanese markets back to fax machines. We've spent a decade concentrating the financial system on three clouds and called it modernization. $MSFT
items.tweetB: Arm's share of hyperscaler servers is 3x since 2024. Every custom CPU that ships is a socket Intel and AMD don't get back. The x86 server franchise is being retired one data hall at a time. $ARM $INTC $AMD

items.title: IAEA has lost track of Iran's uranium stockpile as clerics push to quit the NPT; US strikes Sirik
items.idea: Mando's Macro list: US strikes Sirik, Iran claims a strike on a US radar; the IAEA has lost track of Iran's uranium stockpile; Iran's clerics are pushing to quit the nuclear treaty; Trump would consider strikes on Cuba; Ukraine hit Russia's Volgograd refinery; China staged surprise drills near Taiwan; the Dutch government is near collapse over a wealth tax.
items.angle: 'Lost track of the uranium' plus NPT-exit talk changes the end-state of the Iran conflict from a deal to a proliferation question, which justifies a structurally higher oil and gold premium.
items.tweetA: The IAEA can't find Iran's uranium and Iran's clerics want out of the NPT. That's the moment the conflict stops being about tankers and starts being about a bomb. Gold has been pricing that. Oil hasn't. $GLD $USO
items.tweetB: Same headline list: strikes on Sirik, surprise drills near Taiwan, Ukraine hitting Volgograd, Trump floating Cuba. Four theaters in one morning and VIX barely at 20. The market has stopped pricing geopolitics individually.

items.title: Fed drops its October 2027 meeting from the calendar; Bessent says the debt curve can be bent with growth
items.idea: Also in Mando: the Fed dropped its October 2027 meeting from the calendar; Bessent says the US debt curve can be bent with growth; the 30Y auction tailed as demand faded; the budget deficit hit an all-time high; BofA says shorts are piling into rate-sensitive stocks; Morgan Stanley warns against buying the AI dip.
items.angle: A record deficit, a tailed long-bond auction and a Treasury Secretary arguing growth will fix it is the setup ING calls the 'debasement trade' (see Innes item).
items.tweetA: Record deficit, tailed 30Y auction, and the Treasury's answer is 'we'll grow out of it'. That's the sentence every bond vigilante has been waiting to hear. $TLT
items.tweetB: BofA: shorts piling into rate-sensitive stocks. Morgan Stanley: don't buy the AI dip. When both sides of the Street agree, the pain trade is a rate rally. Worth owning a little.

items.title: Nvidia succession circus: staff urge Jensen's reinstatement, Trump backs Tim Cook, DOJ antitrust probe, SMCI crashes
items.idea: Mando's AI list: Nvidia bounced from the bottom as retail piled in; SMCI crashed as the US probes Alice Huang links; a second affair with a staffer reported; Nvidia staff urging the board to reinstate Jensen; Trump backs Tim Cook as next CEO; US has no proof Alice Huang was a spy; Nvidia faces a DOJ antitrust probe; Senate calls Jensen and Lutnick to testify. Anthropic IPO ~6x oversubscribed; OpenAI raised $15B at $1.25T.
items.angle: Supermicro being caught in the probe means the scandal is moving down the supply chain to server assemblers, the likely conduits for diversion.
items.tweetA: SMCI crashing on Alice Huang links tells you where the investigation is going: not the chip designer, the box assemblers. If you own anything that ships GPUs to Southeast Asia, read your 10-K. $SMCI $NVDA
items.tweetB: Staff want Jensen back, the President wants Tim Cook, the DOJ wants an antitrust case, the Senate wants testimony. Four principals, four answers. That's a governance vacuum at a $3T company heading into earnings. $NVDA

items.title: PPI 6.5% y/y runs ~250bp above CPI; truck freight prices +25% y/y
items.idea: October PPI +0.3% headline and core, in line after +1.4% and +0.8% in September (revised). Y/y: headline 6.5%, core 5%, ~250bp above consumer inflation. Energy flat m/m but +37% y/y; food +1.3% m/m. Core goods +0.5% m/m, 5.2% y/y, led by organic chemicals +3.9%. Truck freight +3.9% m/m and +25% y/y; air freight flat but +6.3% y/y. Machinery/vehicle wholesale margins -4.2%.
items.angle: A 250bp PPI-CPI gap is a margin squeeze for anyone who can't pass through costs. Wholesale margins already compressing is the first sign.
items.tweetA: PPI running 250bp above CPI means someone between the factory and the consumer is eating 2.5 points of margin. Wholesale margins -4.2% in a month tells you who. Q4 earnings will tell you how much.
items.tweetB: Truck freight +25% y/y. That's not energy pass-through anymore, that's capacity. The freight recession is over and nobody updated the inflation model. $ODFL $JBHT

items.title: Anthropic IPO: $70-78 range, ~$1.4-1.5T, ~$90B total raise beats SpaceX's $86.2B
items.idea: Anthropic set a $70-78 range, prices Nov 18 and trades on Nasdaq as ANT on Nov 19. Top of range is ~$1.4T fully diluted; FT reports bankers expect to price above. With a $26B private placement to Google, Nvidia, AMD and other suppliers, total raise is ~$90B vs SpaceX's $86.2B in June. Jay Ritter: average IPO pops 17.7% day one, then trails the market by 20.5pp over three years. S-1 covers margins, compute sourcing, a SpaceX compute deal, 'Anthropic Direct' and four chip suppliers at one table.
items.angle: The placement buyers are its own suppliers. Read the S-1 for the circularity question that just blew up Nvidia's funding web.
items.tweetA: Anthropic's $26B private placement goes to Google, Nvidia and AMD, its compute suppliers. The same week the market discovered it hates circular financing at Nvidia. ANT prices Tuesday. Read the related-party section first.
items.tweetB: Ritter's data: IPOs pop 17.7% then lag the market by 20.5 points over 3 years. The largest raise in history meets the most predictable statistic in finance. I'd rather own the suppliers on the S-1 than the stock. $GOOGL $AMZN

items.title: FT: Arm boss Rene Haas approached in the Nvidia CEO search
items.idea: SixSigmaCapital flagged an FT report that Arm CEO Rene Haas has been approached about the Nvidia CEO role. This sits alongside reports that Trump backs Tim Cook and staff want Jensen reinstated.
items.angle: Haas would be a supply-chain and licensing operator, not a product visionary, and his move would create a succession problem at Arm (SoftBank-controlled) at the moment Arm's hyperscaler share is tripling.
items.tweetA: Nvidia approaching Rene Haas is the most rational name yet: someone who already runs a royalty empire across every hyperscaler. It also tells you the board's priority is supplier and customer diplomacy, not the next architecture. $NVDA $ARM
items.tweetB: If Haas leaves, Arm loses its CEO just as its hyperscaler server share triples. Nobody's pricing the second-order succession risk at $ARM. $SFTBY

items.title: Microsoft outage day two: 365 deployments paused, shares -3%; Cerebras lands a Microsoft cloud deal
items.idea: Outlook, Teams and M365 outage ran into a second day, not fully restored ~17 hours in; Microsoft paused all 365 deployments and configuration changes; shares -3% pre-market. Cerebras announced a Microsoft cloud deal on its Q3 call. Also: Amazon plans to own the world's product data to fight AI shopping agents (Reuters); nonprofits sued Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and SpaceX's AI unit to halt frontier model development; dLocal TPV +77% to $18B; Lilly broke ground on a $3.5B retatrutide plant.
items.angle: Microsoft adding Cerebras while freezing its own deployments: heterogeneous compute is arriving at the biggest buyer, and ops reliability is the cost of scale.
items.tweetA: Amazon wants to own the world's product data to stop AI shopping agents. Translation: the agent that buys for you is a bigger threat to retail margins than any competitor. $AMZN $SHOP
items.tweetB: Microsoft paused every 365 deployment after a 17-hour outage and the same day signed Cerebras for cloud compute. The fleet is getting more heterogeneous and the failure surface is getting bigger. $MSFT $CBRS

items.title: AlphaGenome 2 finds 30% of believed-causal variants vs 16% for v1, conditioned on cell type and state
items.idea: DeepMind's AG2 takes a million DNA letters plus a condition (tissue, cell type, cell state, or data from a few dozen unseen cells) and predicts function there. Trained on 107M+ single-cell profiles from 68 human and mouse tissues. On 28 immune cell types it found 30% of variants scientists believe are causal vs 16% for AG1.
items.angle: GWAS has produced thousands of disease-variant links that never became drugs because nobody knew which gene or cell. Nearly doubling causal hit rate in one generation compresses target ID, the first step in a16z's 'Eroom's law reversal'.
items.tweetA: AlphaGenome went from 16% to 30% of causal variants in one generation. Two more doublings and the bottleneck in genetics-to-drugs moves from 'which target' to 'which chemistry'. Good for drug hunters, bad for target-ID CROs. $GOOGL
items.tweetB: Google dropped AlphaGenome 2 the day Nvidia's CEO resigned. The company with its own chips and its own science models had the best week in tech without anyone noticing. $GOOGL

items.title: argenx buys Unnatural Products for up to $1.15B to put an FcRn biologic into a pill
items.idea: argenx acquires UNP (macrocycle peptides) for $550M upfront plus up to $595M in milestones. They've partnered since last year on an oral pill targeting FcRn, the same target as Vyvgart, which did $1.72B in sales last quarter. Macrocycles promise biologic precision in a pill that can reach intracellular targets.
items.angle: Oral versions of injectable blockbusters are the self-cannibalization defense. Lilly's oral GLP-1 strategy is the same playbook.
items.tweetA: argenx is paying $1.15B to make a pill version of its own $7B-run-rate injectable. When the leader buys the technology that could replace its product, that's the tell the oral-biologic shift is real. $ARGX
items.tweetB: Macrocycles: antibody-level precision, pill-level convenience, intracellular reach. If this works, the moat around every injectable franchise shrinks. Patent cliffs aren't the only risk to biologics anymore. $LLY $NVO

items.title: Path Robotics: $300M at $2.45B, revenue up 17x in 18 months, $600M HII shipbuilding deal
items.idea: Path's Obsidian model looks at each joint, plans a custom weld and adjusts in real time, unlike robots that repeat a fixed path. Series E led by Georgian at $2.45B. Revenue +17x in 18 months; customers include Lockheed, Saronic and HII (Navy shipbuilder, $600M deal). A Boston Dynamics quadruped with Path's tech (Rove) has 50 preorders. Golden-gloves welders can earn ~$1M/year.
items.angle: Welder scarcity is a binding constraint on US shipbuilding and defense reshoring. Physical-AI that removes a labor bottleneck in a defense supply chain gets priced like infrastructure.
items.tweetA: A top welder can make $1M a year and the Navy can't build ships fast enough. Path Robotics revenue up 17x in 18 months is what it looks like when AI hits a labor bottleneck with a defense budget behind it. $HII $LMT
items.tweetB: Everyone watches humanoids. The real physical-AI money is going to narrow, high-skill trades: welding, inspection, pipefitting. Boring tasks with $1M-a-year humans attached.

items.title: SpaceX orders HJT solar cell lines with a plan for 100 GW/year of equipment, enough for ~475,000 Starmind satellites a year
items.idea: SINGULUS announced SpaceX signed a turnkey heterojunction cell line (~€60M) for Bastrop, Texas, delivery 1H27, with plans to scale to 'more than 100 GW of production equipment'. Each Starmind space data center has a 210kW array; 100 GW/yr would supply ~475,000 a year vs ~15,000 active satellites in orbit. McCormick: 'exactly the kind of thing you'd expect to hear if we were in a bubble.'
items.angle: 100 GW/yr is roughly a fifth of global annual solar installs. Even if satellites don't absorb it, a vertically integrated US HJT supplier at that scale would reshape the domestic solar market.
items.tweetA: SpaceX wants equipment for 100 GW a year of solar cells. The whole US installed ~50 GW last year. Either Starmind is real or Elon just became America's largest solar manufacturer by accident. Both outcomes matter for $FSLR.
items.tweetB: €60M of actual orders, a 100 GW press release, and a meaningful bump to SPCX's market cap. That ratio is the tell of where we are in the cycle.

items.title: Voyager 1 passes one light-day from Earth next Wednesday, 49 years after launch
items.idea: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause in 2012 and next week reaches one light-day from home, the farthest human-made object. Still only ~1/34-trillionth of the observable universe's 93B light-year width; at this pace a full crossing takes 1.67 quadrillion years, 120,000x the universe's age.
items.angle: Cultural moment with long shelf life; also a reminder that 1977 engineering is still returning data, the kind of durability no modern spacecraft program optimizes for.
items.tweetA: Voyager 1 hits one light-day from Earth next week, running on 1977 hardware with less memory than a car key fob. We can't keep a cloud email service up for 17 hours. $MSFT
items.tweetB: 49 years to cover one light-day. At this speed, crossing the observable universe takes 120,000x the age of the universe. Every space-economy pitch deck should start with that chart.

items.title: LSD reversed brain-aging gene signatures in rodents, outranking all 193 drugs in a reference database
items.idea: Aging Cell study (Savino, Iorio et al.) mapped prefrontal-cortex gene-expression drift across 3,086 human samples aged 2 days to 106 years. In chronically dosed rats and single-dose mice, LSD opposed the aging signature more strongly than exercise or enriched environments and outranked all 193 drugs in the database. In a dish it repaired amyloid-beta-damaged neurons. MDMA and alcohol pushed brains older.
items.angle: Psychedelic biotechs have traded on depression; a neurodegeneration angle would expand the addressable market by an order of magnitude. Early rodent data, but a narrative catalyst.
items.tweetA: LSD beat all 193 drugs in a reference set at reversing brain-aging gene signatures. If even a fraction translates, the psychedelic sector's TAM moves from depression to Alzheimer's. $CMPS $ATAI
items.tweetB: Same study: alcohol makes brains look older on the gene-expression clock. The most socially accepted drug is the one with the worst result. Expect that line in a lot of policy debates.

items.title: Goldman's China 2027: 4.5% growth from 'less drag', not recovery; CNY to 6.30

Exports keep gaining global share, inflation stays subdued, and GS sees the renminbi strengthening toward 6.30. Risks: 21st Party Congress, US-China relations, local-government finances.
items.angle: A stronger CNY with deflationary exports is an unusual combo: China exporting deflation in dollar terms while its currency rises. Bad for EM manufacturers competing with China, good for US goods inflation.
items.tweetA: Goldman: China grows 4.5% because things get less bad, not better. And the RMB goes to 6.30 anyway. A rising currency with falling export prices means China's export share gains are coming from productivity, not FX. $FXI $CNH

items.title: Key-person risk's flip side: the departing founder becomes the hook for every ignored bear story
items.idea: FTAV: Nvidia has lost $1.6T of market value since early October. Years of reporting on export-control circumvention, the change that moved Singapore from second-largest market to 'other', Culper's May report, vendor financing and off-balance-sheet liabilities were all public. Interest in that reporting 'correlated inversely with total portfolio returns'. The stock has 70+ buy ratings and at most one sell since Feb 2023. Key point: the founder's exit creates a new hook for old stories exactly when the company's defences are weakest.
items.angle: The bear case was public, unchanged and ignored until there was a narrative hook. The opportunity is finding the next company where the bear case is public and only lacks a catalyst.
items.tweetA: Nvidia lost $1.6T in six weeks and almost none of the bear case is new. Singapore moved to 'other', Megaspeed, the guarantees: all public. Markets don't price information, they price narrative hooks. $NVDA
items.tweetB: 70+ buy ratings, one sell, for three years. Sell-side consensus isn't a forecast, it's a measure of how much access costs. Which other megacap has a public bear case waiting for its sex scandal?

Lilly's GLP-1s did ~$17B in Q3 2026, nearly matching Anthropic's quarter; Mounjaro+Zepbound ~$40B in 2025, about Salesforce's revenue. Top 25% of drugs earn ~85% of revenue. Pharma trades at 8-20x P/E (3-7x revenue) and gets almost no credit for its discovery engine; Humira fell from $20B (2022) to $4B (2025) after LOE.
items.angle: If AI makes discovery repeatable, pharma could re-rate from annuity multiples to platform multiples. That's the bull case for LLY trading like a tech company.

items.title: Eroom's law meets frontier models: $90B CRO market, wet-lab demand set to explode, labs entering drug discovery
items.idea: PV cost to develop a drug ~$2B over ~13 years; <5% of candidates reach approval; FDA approves 40-50 novel drugs a year; ~2/3 of big-pharma new drugs come via M&A/licensing. CRO market is $90B ($30B discovery/preclinical, $60B clinical). a16z expects wet-lab demand to explode as candidate generation gets faster and AI labs need training data. Anthropic opened a wet lab and announced its own candidates for neglected diseases; OpenAI acquired Orchestra Bio. Isomorphic has $1.2B (Novartis) and $1.7B (Lilly) milestone deals. Bio x AI is at a 'GPT-3 moment'.
items.angle: If candidates become abundant, the bottleneck shifts to validation: wet labs, lab automation and clinical capacity. That's the picks-and-shovels trade.
items.tweetA: When AI makes drug candidates abundant, the scarce thing becomes the wet lab that tests them. $90B CRO market, about to see its biggest demand shock since COVID. $TMO $CRL $IQV
items.tweetB: Anthropic has a wet lab and its own drug candidates. OpenAI bought a biotech-execution company. The frontier labs aren't selling picks to pharma, they're becoming pharma. That's a direct threat to the 'AI software for drug discovery' startups.

items.title: Independent AI auditors have a recruitment problem: Massachusetts wants catastrophic-risk evals every ~4 months
items.idea: Consensus is forming around independent verification organizations (IVOs) for frontier AI. Massachusetts' Mass Wins Act (in conference) would require annual compliance audits plus independent catastrophic-risk evaluations roughly every four months, 'stronger than any AI safety regulation on the books'. Illinois passed a lighter regime in July; the federal FRONTIER Act includes third-party audits; Reps. Jacobs and Beyer are drafting an IVO bill. Constraint: people. METR's president says capacity, not access, is the binding constraint. OpenAI: 'high level we are concerned about capacity.'
items.angle: The Securities Acts of 1933-34 created the audit industry. Mandated AI audits create a new professional-services market; Accenture is already acquiring into it.
items.tweetA: The 1933 Securities Act created the Big Four. A mandated AI audit regime does the same for model evaluation, and right now the whole talent pool fits in one Berkeley group house. Whoever trains the auditors owns the next compliance industry. $ACN
items.tweetB: METR says its binding constraint isn't lab access, it's staff. Every AI-safety law assumes an auditor exists. If none qualifies, the EU lets companies skip the audit after a 20-day public call. Regulation by vacancy.

items.title: Fat tails, slim ranges: FX turnover is 70x global trade, and equity vol drives FX vol more than bond vol
items.idea: ING estimates global equity and bond holdings at ~300% of world GDP; FX turnover hit ~70x global trade volume in 2025, double the early-1990s ratio. Equity vol has had a more consistent impact on FX vol than bond vol, so an AI-led equity selloff is a more powerful FX catalyst than a policy repricing.
items.angle: Cheap FX vol plus an AI equity drawdown as the biggest tail is an argument for owning JPY/CHF optionality funded by selling expensive equity vol.
items.tweetA: FX turnover is 70x global trade. The currency market is a portfolio-hedging machine with a trade-settlement afterthought. That's why the AI equity trade, not tariffs, is now the biggest FX tail risk. $FXY $FXF

items.title: Dwarkesh now expects AI to match the best human AI researchers by 2028 (25% chance after 2032)

items.angle: If R&D is the AI's own job, compute demand stops scaling with human researcher headcount. Bullish for compute regardless of who runs Nvidia.
items.tweetA: OpenAI's top researchers went from $1K to $7K a day of agent compute in one summer. That's ~$2.5M a year per researcher in inference. When the AI is the R&D team, compute budgets stop scaling with headcount and start scaling with ambition. $NVDA $GOOGL

items.title: 'Spark' vs 'software-only singularity', 50/50: labs already quadruple R&D compute every year just to keep pace
items.idea: Automated researchers would be faster (~10x speed plus round-the-clock, ~50x more work per week), smarter (~80% of a lab's algorithmic progress comes from its top 50 researchers) and more numerous. Countervailing: ideas get harder to find; labs already quadruple R&D compute and double headcount yearly to keep progress constant. If RSI outruns difficulty, a software-only singularity; if not, a 'spark' of 3-6 years of progress in one year, then compute-bound. Dwarkesh: 50/50. Magic matched DeepSeek V4 Pro with half the original GPT-3 compute (~$500K). Global AI compute growing ~3x a year.
items.angle: Even the 'spark' case is compute-bound afterward, so a capabilities jump creates a second wave of demand for fabs, power and robots. The physical layer is the durable trade in both scenarios.
items.tweetA: Labs already quadruple R&D compute every year just to keep progress flat. That's the AI version of Eroom's law, and it's why 'efficiency gains will crush GPU demand' keeps being wrong. $NVDA $TSM
items.tweetB: Dwarkesh's 'spark' case: 4 years of AI progress in 12 months, then everything bottlenecks on chips, fabs and power. Even the conservative scenario ends with a construction boom. $ETN $VRT $AMAT

items.title: Data beats architecture: 3x more pretraining progress from data than models; DeepSeek says synthetic environments drove 'essentially all' RL gains
items.idea: Dwarkesh and Jerry Han found that over six years, more than 3x as much pretraining algorithmic progress came from data improvements as from model improvements. DeepSeek's latest post-training paper: changes to the RL algorithm mattered little; 'systematic improvements in the scale, diversity, and verifiability of synthesized data and environments account for essentially all of the observed gains,' built via automated pipelines. Anthropic's internal CoBench has ~500 real problems its staff solved this year, usable as an RL environment.
items.angle: Value accrues to whoever generates verifiable environments and data, the RL-environment startups and data vendors, rather than to architecture IP.
items.tweetA: DeepSeek: 'essentially all' RL gains came from better synthetic data and environments, not the algorithm. The moat in AI isn't the model architecture. It's the factory that builds the gyms the model trains in.
items.tweetB: 3x more AI progress from data than from model design over six years. Everyone obsesses over who has the best architecture; the real compounding asset is a pipeline that auto-generates harder tests. Bullish on the RL-environment vendors nobody has heard of.
